title: Compatible ordinary Hom, dual and evaluation comparisons
statement: Let X be a scheme, U an open [def-pc-scheme], P an arbitrary cochain complex of modules on the over-U site, and T the degreewise Modules.overEquiv U functor. Write Pprime=T(P), Oprime for the scheme single unit, and Dprime=Hom(Pprime,Oprime) [def-pur-hom-complex]. There is a family b(M):T(Hom(P,M)) isomorphic to Hom(Pprime,T(M)), natural in every chain map M to N. There is an isomorphism d:T(Hom(P,O_U[0])) to Dprime. For every complex F there is an isomorphism t:T(Tot(F tensor Hom(P,O_U[0]))) to Tot(T(F) tensor Dprime), chosen so that for every f satisfying [def-pc-ordinary-evaluation-data], t.inverse;T(f);b(F) satisfies [def-pc-scheme-ordinary-evaluation-formula]. No preservation of quasi-isomorphisms, K-flatness or K-injectivity is assumed or asserted.

proof.text: Use internalHom_overEquiv on every pair of terms and extend across the Hom product projections. Pre- and postcomposition naturality and additivity identify d_M phi minus (-1)^n phi d_P; this gives b(M) and its naturality. At the single unit compose b with Hom(Pprime,-) of the transported-unit chain isomorphism to get d.

Apply the total tensor comparison then tensor with d to get t for each F. Precompose with each tensor summand inclusion and postcompose with each Hom projection. If r+q=0, both formulas curry (y,phi,x) mapped to y*phi(x); reindexing commutes with composition, symmetries, associators, the transported single unit and its unit action. Otherwise both sides are zero. Degree-equality isomorphisms are natural. Product and coproduct universal properties prove the component equation for every f, also for zero complexes and the empty open.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_ordinaryEvaluation_over_comparisons (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (P : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ) :
    let L := Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)
    let T := L.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let P' := T.obj P
    let O' := (HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).obj
      (𝟙_ (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)))
    let D' := homComplex (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) P' O'
    ∃ b : ∀ M : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ,
        T.obj (homComplex (R := X.sheaf.over U) P M) ≅
          homComplex (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) P' (T.obj M),
      (∀ (M N : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ) (a : M ⟶ N),
        T.map (((homComplexFunctor (R := X.sheaf.over U)).obj (op P)).map a) ≫
            (b N).hom =
          (b M).hom ≫
            ((homComplexFunctor (R := U.toScheme.sheaf)).obj (op P')).map (T.map a)) ∧
      ∃ d : T.obj (localEvaluationDual X U P) ≅ D',
        ∀ F : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ,
          ∃ t : T.obj (localEvaluationTensor X U P F) ≅
              pullbackTensorTotal U.toScheme (T.obj F) D',
            ∀ f : localEvaluationTensor X U P F ⟶ homComplex (R := X.sheaf.over U) P F,
              IsLocalOrdinaryEvaluation X U P F f →
                IsSchemeOrdinaryEvaluation U.toScheme P' (T.obj F)
                  (t.inv ≫ T.map f ≫ (b F).hom)
